 NASHVILLE, Tenn. (WZTV) — If you’re behind on your electric bill, assistance may be available. But where you apply, what paperwork you have ready and whether your account is still active can affect your options.
 FOX 17 News contacted NES, NeedLink Nashville and Metro Action to explain how customers can seek help before an overdue bill leads to a disconnection or a closed account.
 PREVIOUS COVERAGE | $765 electric bill leaves Nashville woman in the dark for more than a month 
 The need is widespread. At its Nov. 18 board meeting, NES reported that 19,201 accounts across its service area had a disconnection trigger date between Nov. 12 and Dec. 10. The utility emphasized that a trigger date does not automatically mean service will be disconnected.
 Here’s what customers should know:
 NeedLink: Help paying a past-due bill
 NeedLink provides short-term financial assistance to eligible households. NES recently provided another $500,000 to the organization for utility assistance.
 In a response to FOX 17 News, NeedLink said applicants generally must:
 Have a past-due bill.
 Have household income below 300% of the federal poverty level.
 Not have received assistance through its NES-funded program within the previous six months.
 Applicants should have a photo ID, utility bill and income documentation ready.
 NeedLink says eligibility does not guarantee assistance. Staff must verify documents and account information, and demand is high.
 Online applications normally open at 10 a.m. each business day and close when the organization reaches the number it can process that day. NeedLink recommends applying close to opening time.
 Holiday schedule: During the week of Nov. 23, online applications will open at 10 a.m. Monday through Wednesday only. In-person application assistance will not be available Nov. 23–24 and will resume Nov. 30. Normal in-person hours are Monday and Tuesday, 10 a.m.–2 p.m., at Westminster Presbyterian Church, 3900 West End Avenue, using the Wilson Entrance.
 Questions can be directed to 615-269-6835.
 Apply for NeedLink NES assistance here .
 NeedLink resources Nashville Electric Service customers. If you’re behind on your electric bill, assistance may be available. But where you apply, what paperwork you have ready and whether your account is still active can affect your options. (Photo: FOX 17 News) 
 Metro Action: Energy assistance for Davidson County households
 Metro Action administers the federally funded Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program, known as LIHEAP.
 Applicants must live in Davidson County, meet household income guidelines and satisfy other program requirements. Assistance is generally a one-time award per program year, which runs from Oct. 1 through Sept. 30.
 MORE | NES changes how it brings in extra crews during emergencies after January ice crisis 
 Documents to have ready include:
 Identification for the applicant.
 Social Security cards for household members.
 Proof of household income or required zero-income paperwork.
 The current utility bill.
 A 12-month billing history from the utility company.
 Additional forms may be required for applicants who are self-employed or need disability verification.
 Metro Action’s current application instructions say customers must apply online and have a working email address. People who need computer access or help completing the application can visit the Customer Care Center at 1281 Murfreesboro Pike.
 In-person hours are Monday through Friday, 8 a.m.–3:30 p.m. The call center remains open until 4:30 p.m. at 615-862-8860.
 Start a Metro Action utility assistance application here .
 Assistance for Davidson County households. If you’re behind on your electric bill, assistance may be available. But where you apply, what paperwork you have ready and whether your account is still active can affect your options. (Photo: FOX 17 News) 
 NES: Ask about more time to pay
 Customers who need additional time should call NES Customer Relations at 615-736-6900 to ask about payment extensions or arrangements. NES says an automated arrangement request option is available around the clock.
 When discussing an arrangement, ask:
 How much must I pay?
 When is that payment due?
 What must I do to maintain or restore service?
 NES told FOX 17 News that a payment arrangement spreads out an older balance; it does not erase it. A customer may owe both the current month’s electric charges and an installment on past-due debt.
 The utility also says making a partial payment does not automatically restore disconnected service. NES must review the account and confirm the payment or arrangement required.
 Nashville Electric Service payment options. If you’re behind on your electric bill, assistance may be available. But where you apply, what paperwork you have ready and whether your account is still active can affect your options. (Photo: FOX 17 News) 
 What if your bill is marked “final”?
 A disconnection and a final bill can mean different things when seeking assistance.
 NES says a final bill means service associated with an account has stopped or the account has been closed, and the remaining balance has been calculated.
 RELATED COVERAGE | Did NES understaff? We compared lineworker numbers, and that led to questions 
 Metro Action says its LIHEAP program requires an active account. A disconnected account may still qualify if it remains active, but an account that has been final billed does not meet that requirement.
 NeedLink told FOX 17 News that its online NES-funded program also requires an active account. Customers with final bills should apply in person for an individual review. However, funding for those cases is limited, and customers may need to pay down their balances before assistance can be considered.
 NES says customers with final bills should still contact Customer Relations to review their options.
 Questions about funding and demand
 FOX 17 News has asked NES how much of its $500,000 donation to NeedLink remains available and how long that funding is expected to last.
 We also asked how the current delinquency rate compares with this time last year and a typical year.
 For customers struggling now, NeedLink’s advice is to seek assistance before the account reaches final bill status, when options can become more limited.
